blocks.text: An Indigenous Community in the Chaco and Return to Asunción

provenance.rationale: Uses the Word’s Day 10 heading for the same excursion, with the singular community and Chaco location made explicit in the RU title.

blocks.text: In the morning, you visit an Indigenous community in the Chaco. This part of the trip is devoted to people who lived on this land long before Europeans arrived. You learn about daily life and local crafts and see how the community preserves its history and connection to the land. After visiting Asunción and the Mennonite colonies, you can see how differently people have made a home in the same region. You then visit the Filadelfia Museum. Its exhibits cover the Chaco’s natural environment, Indigenous peoples, Mennonite settlers, the Chaco War and how settlements adapted to heat and water shortages. After lunch, the drive back to Asunción takes about four hours.
